items.title: Zelensky's dangerous gambit to merge the Iran and Ukraine Wars
items.summary: As Ukraine’s Volodymyr Zelensky arrives in Washington, much indicates that he is no longer merely trying to draw greater American support into its war against Russia. Increasingly, it appears to be pursuing something far more consequential: merging the Ukraine war with the U.S.-Iran conflict into a single strategic theater. The distinction matters. If the two wars become one, Ukraine ceases to be merely a recipient of American military assistance and instead becomes a direct participant in Washington's war with Tehran. By the same token, the United States would no longer simply be Ukraine's principal arms supplier. It would become an active belligerent against Russia through a conflict that stretches from the Black Sea to the Caspian. For Kyiv, this would represent the strategic breakthrough it has sought since Russia's invasion in 2022. items.title: Zelensky's big idea for Trump: Ukraine is the Israel of Europe
items.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky landed in Washington with a bang Tuesday, just days after Ukraine carried out a missile strike against an Iranian cargo ship in the Caspian Sea. The attack appears to be part of Zelensky’s effort to win over President Donald Trump, who has long had a tense relationship with the Ukrainian leader. The pitch is simple: Ukraine is the kind of partner who will take action when others won’t. US President Donald Trump earlier proposed using Tehran’s blocked funds to cover damage to ships and cargo in the waterway. Iran denounced the proposal as “incendiary”. Iran’s Khatam al-Anbiya Central Headquarters, which oversees the unified command of the country’s armed forces, said the restrictions would apply to “All companies and countries that welcome Trump’s proposal and use Iran’s blocked assets”. The command described Trump’s threat as an “illegal action.”

"We'll be hitting that area very probably pretty soon. And there’s not a thing they can do about it," Trump said on Tuesday, as the US continued its attacks on Iran. Tehran warned that any strike on its nuclear facilities would widen the regional war. Israel says Iran transferred enriched uranium and advanced centrifuges to the mountain after US and Israeli attacks damaged other nuclear sites. It has provided no evidence, and Trump acknowledged that Washington could not confirm the assertion. Here is what we know about the facility. items.title: 'Trump Needs a Way Out of This War': Michel Yakovleff explains 'charade' over US-Iran negotiations
items.summary:
Eve Irvine is pleased to welcome General Michel Yakovleff, Professor at Sciences-Po and Former Vice-Chief of Staff at NATO's Supreme Headquarters Allied Powers Europe (Shape).. He presents a strategic rather than tactical reading of the current lull in the US-Iran conflict. He argues that the apparent de-escalation is not evidence of diplomatic progress but of mounting structural constraints. Rather than viewing pauses in hostilities as signs of imminent peace, he frames them as consequences of political pressure, military logistics and industrial limitations.
 
At the centre of his argument is the proposition that modern warfare is ultimately governed by sustainability. Missile stockpiles, industrial production capacity, domestic political legitimacy and alliance commitments become as decisive as battlefield success. General Yakovleff contends that the United States retains ample military capability to continue operations against Iran in isolation, yet doing so progressively erodes its ability to deter other adversaries, reassure allies and sustain global commitments.

items.title: Islamic Resistance in Iraq denies it carried out strikes on Saudi oil facilities
items.summary: Islamic Resistance in Iraq denies it carried out strikes on Saudi oil facilities The Islamic Resistance in Iraq rejected allegations that it carried out drone attacks on oil facilities in Saudi Arabia. Earlier, Riyadh accused "Iranian-backed militias" for the strikes on Monday. The network of Iran-aligned groups said the allegation "only strengthens our conviction that hostility towards Iraq and its people is an inherent characteristic of this regime". "These fabrications are nothing but an attempt to justify their inability to respond to the painful Yemeni strikes that have targeted the heart of their infrastructure," it added, warning that any "foolish action" by the kingdom would be met with a "harsh response".
